BENGALURU (SCCH-2), PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the petitioners have challenged the judgment and award dated 22.10.2019 passed in M.V.C.No.1826/2018 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru (SCCH-2) ('the Tribunal'
for short).
2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, the husband of petitioner No.1 and father of petitioner No.2 by name K.T.Krishnappa, the deceased, while riding motor cycle bearing No.KA-51/EG-2163 on 17.03.2018 at about 11.50 a.m., near APS Diploma NC: 2023:KHC:41298 College Gate, Somanahalli, Uttarahalli Hobli, on NH- 29, Bangalore, hit by another motor cycle bearing No.KA-41/EJ-0215 from behind injuring him.

He was treated at Government Hospital, Kaggalipura and at NIMHANS, Bangalore,
but he succumbed to injuries.
The petitioners being the dependants have approached the Tribunal seeking grant of compensation of Rs.20 lakhs.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.
After taking the evidence, the Tribunal awarded Rs.5,30,000/- with interest @ 9% per annum.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement of compensation, the petitioners have filed this appeal on various heads.

4. Heard the arguments of Smt.V.Nithya, learned counsel on behalf of Sri M.H.Prakash for the petitioners and Sri.B.C.Shivanne Gowda, learned counsel on behalf of Sri.B.Pradeep, for Insurance Company.
NC: 2023:KHC:41298 5.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the deceased was aged 58 years,
running a canteen at APS Diploma College, he was earning Rs.18,000/- per month, but the Tribunal Smt. Vijayalakashmi vs Bharathi Axa Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49479677/
2 did not consider it and assessed the notional income at Rs.10,000/- and awarded the compensation on the lower side and sought for enhancement.
6.

entities.text: Smt. Vijayalakashmi vs Bharathi Axa Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that before the Tribunal except the letter issued by the APS Polytechnic, there is no other material explaining the avocation of the deceased as a caterer in the Polytechnic.
There is no licence by the BBMP and there is no proof of income to show the earning of Rs.18,000/- per month.
The Tribunal has rightly assessed the income at Rs.10,000/-, there is no need for enhancement, he supported the impugned judgment and sought for dismissal of the appeal.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of the parties and perused the records.
8. The accident took place on account of the offending motor cycle hitting on the back side of the motor cycle of the deceased.

Hence, there is no scope for contributory negligence and only the wife is entitled to claim compensation as she alone is dependant and second petitioner being major son aged 36 years cannot be a dependant.
The accident is of the year 2018.
Even taking into consideration the fact that there is no proof of income, a person with such avocation will earn not less than Rs.12,500/- per month.
Hence, income assessed by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

9. In a case of this nature, compensation has to be determined by following the principles settled by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance NC: 2023:KHC:41298 Co.Ltd. -vs- Pranay Sethi and Others1 and Sarla Varma (Smt.) and Others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation and Another2 so also the principle laid down in Shri Ram General Insurance Co. Ltd. - Vs- Bhagat Singh Rawat & Ors.3 10.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
By applying these principles, there is no scope for future prospects as he was aged 63 years,
taking income at Rs.12,500/- per month, the applicable multiplier is '7', then the loss of dependency will be: Rs.12,500/- - Rs.4,166/- (1/3rd) = Rs.8,334/- x 12 x 7 = Rs.7,00,056/-.

Towards loss of consortium to the wife at Rs.40,000/-, loss of love and affection to petitioner No.2 at Rs.50,000/-;
towards funeral expenses and loss of estate at Rs.15,000/- each, amounting to Rs.1,20,000/-.

Since the claim is of the year 2018, in view of the judgment in Bhagat Singh Rawat's case (supra), 10%
appreciation for each 3 years if added, it comes (2017) 16 SCC 680 (2009) 6 SCC 121 Civil Appeal Nos.2410-2412/2023, decided on 27.03.2023 NC: 2023:KHC:41298 to Rs.12,000/-.
Then the compensation under conventional heads comes to Rs.1,32,000/-.
Totally, the petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.8,32,056/- as against Rs.5,30,000/- assessed by the Tribunal.

Hence,
petitioners are entitled for enhancement of Rs.3,02,056/-, which is the just compensation to which the petitioners are entitled.
Hence, the appeal merits consideration.

In the result, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
